name: Forehand loop against backspin
summary: Lift a backspin ball with a brushing, upward swing driven by your legs.
whenToUse: Against a long push or long backspin serve to your forehand. It's the main way to start your attack.

keyPoints.stance: Wider than for the drive, right foot further back (left foot if left-handed), knees well bent, weight on the back leg.
keyPoints.bodyAction: Legs push up and the hips and shoulders turn forward. Weight moves from the back leg to the front leg.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Longer than the drive and more upward: from about knee height to above your head.
keyPoints.timing: At the top of the bounce or just as it starts to drop. Beginners: a little after the top gives you more time.
keyPoints.tablePosition: About a metre from the end line.
keyPoints.freeArm: Up for balance, then pulls back as you turn into the shot.
keyPoints.batArm: Relaxed and fairly long at the start; speed up sharply at contact. Bat about vertical or slightly closed.
keyPoints.recovery: Reset your legs and get back to ready fast: a block comes back quickly.
keyPoints.anticipation: Read the length of their push early. Long push to the forehand = loop.

cues: Drop the bat under the ball
Contact as it starts to drop

learningPath.task: Watch the 3D player in slow motion. Notice how low the bat starts and how the legs start the swing.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along mode: deep knee bend, low bat, swing up and forward.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did the bat start below the height of the table?
Did your legs push before your arm swung?
Did you finish above your head and come back to ready?

learningPath.task: Slow backspin balls one at a time. Just lift them onto the table, any speed.
Sets of 10 loops; aim for depth and spin, not speed.
Push, then loop the long ball.
Serve short backspin, loop the long push.
learningPath.passCheck: 6 of 10 third balls on the table.

gamePatterns.situation: You serve short backspin and they push long.
gamePatterns.how: Loop it with spin to their elbow or backhand. Spin first, speed second.

gamePatterns.situation: A long push comes to your forehand in a push rally.
gamePatterns.how: Open up with a spinny loop deep to their backhand, then get ready for the block.

troubleshooting.symptom: The ball goes into the net
causes: Not lifting enough against the backspin
fixes: Bend your knees and meet the ball a bit earlier

causes: The push had less backspin than you read
fixes: Against light backspin, close the bat a little
Brush the back of the ball thinly, more up than forward
Start with the legs and hips
Relax, then speed up sharply right at contact

troubleshooting.symptom: I'm off balance after the loop
fixes: Finish with your weight on the front leg

penholdNotes: Same legs and body. Penholders tend to use more wrist; keep it under control until the shape is solid.
